schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The == compare, living in exactly one place. A gate holds a findings report and an allowlist and OPENS when they are IDENTICAL — not a subset, not within tolerance, not a judge's opinion. `verdict(findings, allowed)` returns OPEN/CLOSED plus the diff in BOTH directions: `unexpected` (fired but not allowed) and `missing` (allowed but did not fire). ONE THING IS NORMALIZED AND ONLY ONE: findings are compared as canonical JSON, SORTED — because without sorting the gate measures the scanner's iteration order rather than its findings, and a filesystem walk in a different order would close a gate that found exactly what it was supposed to find. Duplicates are NOT collapsed; the compare is a multiset compare, so a scanner that starts double-firing is caught rather than deduplicated into looking correct. IT HOLDS NO STATE — findings and allowlist both arrive as arguments, nothing is remembered between calls, which is why it is a tool and not a machine (Law 6). It contains no branch that could consult anything: the primitive that makes 'no gate consults an oracle' enforceable cannot itself be the exception.
why: Akien, 2026-08-13, verbatim, and it is the entire specification: 'NO GATES MAY CONSULT ORACLES EVER PERIOD. A GATE ONLY OPENS WHEN A FINDINGS REPORT MATCHES WHAT IT ALLOWS. ITS AN == compare. Must be identical. NO ORACLE.' THE LIVED SYMPTOM this ends: gate-ness lived in PROSE. build_inspector's charter said it was a gate and said gates are inference-free; `cairn determinism` could report where the LLM was but could not red a gate for reaching one, because nothing on disk said which components WERE gates. A rule you have to remember to apply is a rule that is not enforced (Law 4). Berthing the compare in one importable module turns gate-ness into an IMPORT FACT — a gate is a component that reaches this — which the same walk that finds the LLM can read. Two import facts, one walk, and an absolute rule becomes physics. WHY IDENTICAL AND NOT SUBSET, which is the reading everyone reaches for first: a subset compare makes the allowlist a PERMISSION SLIP that can only ever be too generous, and it goes stale in the direction that looks safe — the day a finding stops firing, the gate keeps allowing it and nobody learns the world changed. Identity makes the allowlist a SPECIFICATION OF THE EXPECTED STATE, so a finding that disappears closes the gate exactly as loudly as one that appears. That is Law 9 turned into a compare: green is earned every run, never inherited from whenever somebody last wrote the list.
invoke: `from cairn.tools.gate import gate` — `gate.verdict(findings, allowed)` for the full answer, `gate.opens(findings, allowed)` for the boolean. No CLI door: a gate is composed by the component doing the gating, never run at a person. `cairn determinism` reports which components reach it and reds any that also reach an oracle. Prove: `python3 cairn/tools/gate/proofs/test_gate.py`.
node_class: tool — a complete primitive with USERS, not an owner (Law 6, ruling 2026-08-13-tools-have-users-not-owners). It holds no state, so there is nothing for an owner to gate. Its users so far: cairn/machines/build_inspector.
entry: FRESH build, 2026-08-13, hours after Akien's ruling. Nothing was grafted; the compare it replaces was already in the corpus, written longhand as `clean: not findings` inside build_inspector — the same == against an empty allowlist, spelled out where nothing could see it was a gate. This did not invent the gate, it gave the existing one an address (Law 5).
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter.
how_it_learns: IT DOESN'T, AND THAT IS THE POINT — this is the one component in the system where learning would be the defect. A gate that adjusts what it allows is a gate that opens on something other than an == compare, which is precisely what Akien forbade. What learns is the ALLOWLIST, and it learns by a human writing it down after looking; the compare stays fixed. If a gate's questions need to get better — and Akien expects they will ('We might have to add more or better inspection questions, but that's fine. we learn as we go') — that learning belongs to the INSPECTOR that produces the findings, which may hold a SLEEP seam. The inspector may be MOSTLY DETERMINISTIC; the gate must be PURE. That split is the whole architecture and this module is the half that does not move.
filed_edges: (a) THE ALLOWLIST HAS NO HOME YET. `allowed` arrives as an argument, and build_inspector reads an optional allowed.json beside itself. Nothing yet says where a gate's baseline berths in general, nothing dates it, and nothing records WHO looked at a finding and decided it was allowed. An allowlist entry without that is a green somebody granted and nobody signed.

(b) A FINDING'S IDENTITY IS ITS WHOLE BODY. Two findings differing only in a volatile field (a count, a timestamp, a path rendered differently) are different findings, so a gate over findings that carry volatile fields will never open. That is correct behaviour for an identity compare and a real constraint on what a finding may contain — the discipline lands on the INSPECTOR, and it will be felt the first time a real allowlist is written.
(c) NO CLI DOOR, DELIBERATELY. There is nothing a person would run this at. If one is ever wanted, it is `cairn determinism` growing a `--gates` view, not a second door here.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_gate.py (9 teeth, aimed at the LOOSENINGS an == compare accumulates, not at equality itself). Durability gate: committed + pushed.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a subset opens the gate; (2) an allowed finding that did not fire is not reported missing; (3) duplicates are collapsed; (4) scan order changes a verdict; (5) an empty allowlist opens against a non-empty report; (6) a missing allowlist FILE is read as 'anything goes' rather than as empty — a gate that fails open on an absent baseline is the vacuous green this whole line of work exists to end; (7) an odd finding raises instead of closing, because a raising gate fails open inside any caller that wraps it; (8) a prior call changes a later verdict, which would make this a machine that needs an owner. WRONG-SHAPE SIGNAL: any argument added to `opens` beyond findings and allowed. A tolerance, a mode, a severity floor — each is the compare becoming an opinion.
proof: proofs/test_gate.py — nine teeth. The load-bearing ones are (d) a subset does NOT open it and (e) a MISSING allowed finding closes it too; between them they pin identity against the two directions it decays in. Enforcement of the rule itself lives at determinism's proof (teeth l, l2, m, n, o, p, q), which the corpus runs — including q, which asserts gates EXIST before asserting none consults an oracle, because a rule over an empty set is a green that means nothing.
owner: A TOOL HAS USERS, NOT AN OWNER (Law 6). Akien owns the definition — the == compare and the absolute rule over gates are his words, ruled 2026-08-13. CC writes the code and the proofs.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics — this is the physics under 'no gate consults an oracle', replacing the prose IOU)
Law 9 (red is the default; an identity compare cannot inherit a green from the last run)
Law 7 (a gate's verdict is permanent in a record of truth, so it must replay — which is why a gate may not even have a SLEEP seam)
Law 1 (the compare lives once; build_inspector's longhand `not findings` was the same compare re-derived)
Law 6 (holds no state, so it has users and not an owner)
provenance: Born 2026-08-13 from one sentence of Akien's, given after `cairn determinism` reported where every LLM was and then had to admit it could not red the thing he actually cared about: 'NO GATES MAY CONSULT ORACLES EVER PERIOD.' Its first run caught two things immediately — that it had no charter and so did not exist to its own roster, and that reading gate-ness TRANSITIVELY made skills/chart a gate (it can reach build_inspector) and then red it for a SLEEP seam a skill is entitled to. Gate-ness is a DIRECT import: a gate is what does the compare, not what calls one. Pinned as tooth (l2).
